text:
aj: Heads-up — saw dropped traces when we restart the python inference-worker. OTLP exporter seems to lose in-flight spans on SIGTERM. Repro: send a bunch of requests, then `kill -TERM` — end_span missing for many requests.

maria: Which exporter config? otlp/http or grpc?

aj: otlp/http with default BatchSpanProcessor. exporter timeout 10s.

sam: We hit something similar in Rust last week, turned out the runtime shutdown raced with the background exporter thread.

leo: Key detail: inference workers have long-lived KV cache and continuous batching. Shutdown often happens during a long batch flush => spans buffered but not flushed. Buffer size + shutdown timeout = lost spans.

katie: Can you paste the minimal repro + config?

aj: Sure — python snippet:

```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.http.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor

provider = TracerProvider()
exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint="https://telemetry.rwd.dev/v1/traces")
provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter))
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)

# main inference loop ...
# SIGTERM handler calls: provider.shutdown()
```

maria: provider.shutdown() should flush but BatchSpanProcessor has max_export_batch_size + schedule_delay_millis. If shutdown happens before scheduled export, some spans may still be dropped unless force_flush() called.

sam: In Rust we called `opentelemetry::global::shutdown_tracer_provider();` — but we also had to increase exporter timeout and call force_flush.

leo: Two proposals: 1) change SDK wrapper to call force_flush() with a short timeout in our SIGTERM handler; 2) expose a telemetry drain hook in the serving runtime that waits up to X ms for exporters.

aj: I tried adding a synchronous span processor for shutdown path (SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter)) and it fixed the repro locally, but that increases blocking latency on normal shutdown which we don't want in prod.

katie: Maybe do hybrid: keep BatchSpanProcessor for steady-state, but on SIGTERM swap in SimpleSpanProcessor or call force_flush with backoff and extend shutdown window. Also increase OTLP exporter timeout only for shutdown path.

maria: Also worth auditing how many spans we create per request. Inference path creates spans per token and reranker spans; heavy cardinality + high QPS means buffers fill and schedule hits. Sampling/aggregation might help a lot.

sam: Agreed. For languages: make the instrumentation wrapper provide a common shutdown helper (`redwood_otel::shutdown(timeout_ms)`) so each service doesn't reimplement. PR suggestion: middleware into runtime that listens for SIGTERM and calls into the SDK wrapper.

infra-bot: deploy/12345 failed: job timed out during graceful shutdown (see https://ci.rwd.dev/12345) :warning:

leo: That CI failure is the pattern — the integration test tears down quickly. We should add forced telemetry flush to the teardown so tests don't flake.

aj: Action items:
- aj: open issue with minimal repro + logs (https://rwd.dev/issue/2147)
- maria: draft SDK wrapper changes for py/go/rust (force_flush + timeout)
- sam: add shutdown hook in runtime to call the wrapper, ensure it only runs once per process
- katie: evaluate sampling defaults for inference path to reduce buffer pressure

katie: One more note — telemetry retention/exporter retries interplay: if exporter backend is slow, retries + buffer will fill; we need clear metrics/alerts (buffer_dropped_spans, exporter_retries) in console.

aj: Thanks — I'll paste logs + quick flame graph in the issue. :thumbsup:
